pricing.billingNote: Non-profit public digital library funded by donations and grants.
pricing.freeTierNote: Unlimited HTTP downloads, Torrents, IA S3 CLI access, and in-browser BookReader/Audio playback.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Crowdsourced uploads ranging from pristine 16" ET FLAC rips to 5th-gen 32 kbps MP3 cassette dubs
provenance.airdateMethodology: Uploader-supplied filenames (YY-MM-DD); mixes OTRR Certified research with unverified trader logs
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Free-text item description box; no structured episode-level cast or character schema
provenance.captionEngine: Scattered OCR/auto-ASR on select items; >92% of OTR audio items lack synchronized .vtt files

specNotes.uuid_index: Uses uploader-chosen folder slugs (/details/{slug}) with 50–500 MP3s bundled into one item; no per-broadcast canonical UUID.
specNotes.sha256_dedup: File-level MD5/SHA1 per upload bucket, but identical broadcasts are duplicated across dozens of overlapping uploader items.
specNotes.vtt_subtitles: Over 95% of OTR audio files have no .vtt caption track.
specNotes.schema_jsonld: No Schema.org RadioEpisode JSON-LD markup on item pages.

primary_source_verification.summary: OTRR Certified uploads include researcher log PDFs, but thousands of older user uploads rely on unverified 1990s trader filenames.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Metadata is user-contributed per item; single episodes frequently appear across 6+ items with conflicting YY-MM-DD filename prefixes."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Item-level XML (`_meta.xml`) applies to whole 200-episode ZIP buckets rather than individual episodes or character roles.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Creator and description tags live at the collection/item container level, not per MP3 track inside a multi-file upload."

vtt_transcripts.summary: No systematic WebVTT caption corpus across OTR collections; web player streams raw MP3/Ogg without synchronized dialogue text.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Audio items contain derivative .mp3 and .ogg files plus waveform .pngs, with no synchronized .vtt track derivatives."

master_provenance.summary: Hosts some extraordinary direct 16" transcription disc transfers (e.g., AFRS, NBC, Goldin/Marr donations) alongside undocumented 32k re-encodes.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Includes lossless 16-bit/44.1kHz and 24-bit/96kHz FLAC transfers when uploaded by preservationists, mixed with legacy 32 kbps MP3s."

serial_continuity.summary: Works when filenames strictly obey `YYMMDD_Ep#` sorting inside a single item, but breaks when episodes span multiple uploader items.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Track order in the JWPlayer playlist depends entirely on ASCII sorting of filenames in `_files.xml`."

open_api_export.summary: Full `ia` CLI, Advanced Search JSON API, S3-like bucket URLs (`/download/<item>/`), and torrent manifests.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Internet Archive Metadata API (`/metadata/{identifier}`) exposes full file lists, SHA1/MD5 hashes, and direct HTTP download links."

ad_free_playback.summary: 100% free and ad-free, though high-file-count items experience slow playlist DOM initialization.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "No commercial ads or paywalls; occasional rate-limiting or maintenance downtime during peak archive crawls."

dedup_integrity.summary: Zero cross-item deduplication; the same *Suspense* or *Shadow* recording is routinely duplicated 8 to 15 times across different uploader buckets.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Each uploader creates an independent item identifier (`OTRR_Suspense_Singles`, `suspense-otr`, `Suspense_1942-1962`), resulting in massive duplication."

gotchas.title: Container-Level Metadata Granularity Trap
gotchas.detail: Because an Internet Archive 'Item' often holds 100 to 600 MP3 files, item-level metadata (`_meta.xml`) cannot express per-episode air dates, cast lists, or synopses.

gotchas.title: High-Latency Playlist Boot on Large Items
gotchas.detail: Opening an IA item page with 500+ MP3s + derivatives forces the browser to parse megabytes of playlist JSON before first audio frame playback.

gotchas.title: Derivative Re-Encoding Artifacts
gotchas.detail: IA's automated derivative pipeline historically generated 64k VBR MP3 and Ogg derivatives from already-lossy 32k–64k MP3 uploads, compounding generational artifacts if users stream the derivative instead of the original.
